title: God's Wisdom vs. Clout Chasers
paragraphs: Yo, these are the wise words from Solomon, who was King David's son and the king of Israel. He wrote this stuff down so we can learn how to live a good life, understand the big picture, and know what's up. It's basically a life manual for doing the right thing, being fair, and acting justly. It helps clueless people learn the ropes and gives young people a reality check. Even wise, experienced folks can learn a thing or two from this. It's some next-level wisdom to really get your head around.
The first step to getting smart is respecting God. Only fools would ignore that kind of wisdom and knowledge.

Listen up, my friend, and pay attention to what your dad tells you. Don't forget the lessons you learned from your mom. Their advice is like a crown of victory or some serious bling on your fingers. My dude, if your sketchy friends try to get you to do dumb stuff, just don't. If they're like, "Yo, let's go cause some trouble, beat up some old guy, mug some old woman. Let's pick them clean and get them ready for their funerals. We'll load up on top-quality loot and haul it home by the truckload. Join us—with us, it's share and share alike,"—for real, don't even give them the time of day. They're heading for a bad ending and will mess up everything they touch. You wouldn't rob a bank in broad daylight, right? Well, that's basically what they're doing to themselves. When you're all about getting more and more, you actually become less of a person.
Lady Wisdom is out in the streets, shouting for everyone to hear. She's making a speech in the town square. She's standing in the middle of traffic, at the busiest intersection, calling out:

"You simpletons! How long are you gonna stay clueless? You cynics! How long are you gonna keep that negative attitude? You idiots! How long will you refuse to learn? Turn your life around! I can give you a fresh start. Look, I'm ready to pour out my spirit on you and tell you everything I know. But I've been calling out, and you've been ignoring me. I've reached out, but you've shut me out."

"Since you just laugh at my advice and think my guidance is a joke, how am I supposed to take you seriously? I'll be the one laughing when you're in trouble! What if your whole world comes crashing down? What if a disaster hits and your life is a total wreck? You'll need me then. You'll call for me, but I won't answer. You can look all you want, but you won't find me."

"Because you hated knowledge and didn't want anything to do with fearing God, because you wouldn't take my advice and ignored all my offers to help you, well, you made your bed, now lie in it. You wanted to do your own thing—so how's that working out for you? Don't you see what happens, you simpletons, you idiots? Being careless will get you killed; being complacent is basically suicide. If you listen to me, then you can chill. You can relax now—you're in good hands."

title: How to Not Get Played
paragraphs: My friend, for real, take what I'm saying to heart. Lock in on my advice and protect it like it's your most valuable possession. Actually listen for wisdom, and make it your goal to really understand things. Seriously, if you make insight your number one priority and don't give up, hunting for it like buried treasure, I promise you'll get what it means to have a healthy respect for God. You'll actually start to know Him.

Here's the deal: God is the one who gives out wisdom. He doesn't hide knowledge or understanding. He's got a huge stash of common sense for people who are trying to live right, and he's like a personal bodyguard for those who are real and sincere. He watches over everyone who's trying to be honest and gives extra protection to the ones who are loyal to him.

So once you get this, you'll be able to see what's right and fair, and find the best paths in life. Wisdom will be like your best friend, and knowledge will be your cool companion. Good sense will be your lookout, and insight will watch your back. They'll keep you from taking wrong turns or following the terrible advice of people who are already lost themselves—so lost they can't even tell a road from a tumbleweed. You know, the losers who think being evil is a game and celebrate doing messed-up things. They're on a path to nowhere, just wandering around in circles.

This wisdom will also save you from the player, the smooth-talker who tries to trap you. The one who cheated on her partner and completely forgot the promises she made to God. Her lifestyle is a dead end; every step she takes is one step closer to hell. Anyone who gets with her never seems to make it back to a good life.

So, stick with good people. Keep your feet on the paths that have been proven to be good. The people who live with integrity are the ones who will last and build a good life here. The corrupt ones will be wiped out, and the dishonest will be gone for good.

title: The Ultimate Life Hack Guide
paragraphs: Yo, my friend, don't just forget everything I've taught you. Like, actually take my advice to heart. It'll help you live a super long and awesome life, for real.
Never let go of Love and Loyalty. Keep them close, like a chain around your neck. Tattoo them on your heart. That's how you get a good rep with God and with people.

Trust God with your whole heart. Don't try to figure everything out on your own. Listen for God's voice in everything you do, everywhere you go. He's the one who'll keep you on the right path. Don't get cocky and think you know it all. Run to God! Run from all the bad stuff! Your body will literally glow with health, and you'll feel alive down to your bones! Honor God with everything you have; give him the first and the best of what you've got. Your barns will be bursting at the seams, your wine vats brimming over. But hey, don't get mad when God has to correct you; don't get all sulky about it. He does it because he loves you, just like a dad who's super proud of his kid.

You're seriously blessed when you find Lady Wisdom and become friends with Madame Insight. She's worth way more than any amount of money in the bank; being her friend is better than a huge paycheck. She's more valuable than all the fancy stuff you could ever want; nothing even comes close. With one hand she gives you a long life, and with the other, she gives you respect. She's got a beautiful way about her, and her life is just so complete. She's like the Tree of Life to anyone who hangs on to her. Hold on tight—and you'll be blessed!
God used Lady Wisdom to create the Earth, and with Madame Insight, he set up the heavens. They knew exactly when to make rivers and springs flow, and when to make the dew fall from the sky at night.

My friend, hold on to Clear Thinking and Common Sense for dear life; don't lose sight of them for a second. They'll keep your soul alive and well, and they'll keep you looking good. You'll be able to go about your life safely, without getting tired or tripping up. You'll be able to chill and take naps without a worry in the world, and you'll sleep great at night. No need to freak out over every little thing, or when people say the world is ending. Because God will be right there with you; he'll keep you safe and sound.

Never just walk away from someone who needs help; you're God's hands for that person. Don't tell your neighbor 'maybe later' or 'hit me up tomorrow' when you've got the cash right there in your pocket. Don't try to scam your neighbor when they're just sitting there, trusting you.

Don't walk around with a chip on your shoulder, always looking for a fight. Don't try to be like those people who just push their way through life. Why be a bully? You might ask, 'Why not?' Because God can't stand people with twisted minds. He respects those who are straightforward and honest.

God's curse is on the house of the wicked, but he blesses the home of the righteous. He'll give proud doubters the cold shoulder, but if you're down on your luck, he's right there to help you out. Living wisely gets you honor; living foolishly just makes you look like a clown.

title: The Ultimate Guide to a Goated Life
paragraphs: Aight, listen up, my crew. Your dad's dropping some real talk, so tune in if you wanna know how to actually live. I'm giving you solid advice, so don't just let it go in one ear and out the other.

Back when I was a kid, my dad's favorite and my mom's pride and joy, he'd sit me down and basically drill this into my head: "Lock this in your heart. Do what I say—and you'll live! Drop everything and get that Wisdom! Go hunt for some Understanding! Don't you forget a single word I'm telling you. Don't even drift a little bit. Never walk away from Wisdom—she's your life's bodyguard. Love her, and she'll always have your back. For real, above all else, do this: Get Wisdom! Put this at the very top of your to-do list: Get Understanding! Embrace her, and trust me, you won't regret it. Never let her go—she'll make your life epic. She'll deck out your life with grace and make your days beautiful."

My dude, for real, take my advice; it'll add years to your life. I'm laying out the GPS directions to Wisdom Way, drawing you a map to the Road of Righteousness. I don't want you getting stuck in dead-end streets or wasting your time taking wrong turns. Hold on tight to good advice; don't loosen your grip. Guard it like your life depends on it—because it does! Don't even think about taking the Wicked Bypass; don't even step a foot on that road. Stay way clear of it; give it a ton of space. Take a detour and just keep it moving.

Evil people are lowkey restless unless they're stirring up trouble. They can't even get a good night's sleep unless they've made someone's life miserable. Messing things up is like their food and drink, and violence is their drug of choice.

The path of people living right glows with light; the longer they live, the brighter it shines. But the road of people doing wrong just gets darker and darker—they can't see a thing and end up falling flat on their faces.

My friend, listen up close to what I'm saying; really tune your ears to my voice. Keep my message right in front of you at all times. Focus up! Learn it by heart! People who find these words truly live, like for real live; they're bursting with health, body and soul.

Keep a super close watch on your heart; that's where your whole life gets its start. Don't be two-faced; ditch the careless talk, the little white lies, and all the gossip. Keep your eyes locked straight ahead; ignore all the crazy distractions on the side. Watch where you're going, and the road ahead will smooth out for you. Don't look right or left; just leave all that evil stuff in the dust.

title: Don't Fall for the Trap Queen
paragraphs: Ayo, listen up. I'm about to drop some serious wisdom, so pay attention. This is the real deal, and if you listen, you'll learn how to make good choices and stay out of drama.

This girl might seem super sweet and her words are like honey, but trust me, it's a trap. Before you know it, you'll be left with a bitter taste, a whole lot of pain, and a broken heart. She's on a one-way trip to destruction, and she's trying to take you with her. She's clueless about what's real and has no idea what she's doing with her life.

So for real, my dude, listen up and don't just brush this off. Stay far away from a girl like that, like, don't even go near her part of town. You don't want to throw away your awesome life and waste it on people who couldn't care less about you. Why let randoms use you and take what's yours? You don't want to look back at your life with a bunch of regrets, just a mess of bad choices, thinking, 'Man, I should've listened. Why was I so stubborn? Why didn't I pay attention to the people who were trying to help me? Now my life is a wreck and I have nothing to show for it.'
There's a saying: 'Drink from your own rain barrel, draw water from your own spring-fed well.' It's true. If you don't, you'll come home to find your barrel empty and your well polluted.

Your own 'spring water' is for you and you only, not for everyone to have a sip. Be grateful for your own fountain. Love the person you married when you were young. She's amazing, like an angel and a rose. Never stop taking delight in her, and never take her love for granted. Why would you give up something real and lasting for a cheap thrill with someone who doesn't care about you?

And for real, God sees everything you do. He knows every move you make. Your bad choices will catch up to you and you'll be tripping over your own feet in the dark. A life without self-control leads to death. Your dumb decisions will trap you in a dead end.

title: Don't Be a Fool: Life Hacks from Proverbs 6
paragraphs: Yo, my friend, if you've co-signed a loan for your neighbor or gotten tangled up in a deal with someone you barely know, and you've basically promised your life away and are now stressing big time, listen up. Don't just sit there, you gotta get out of that mess ASAP. You're basically in their control! Go, look desperate, beg if you have to. Don't wait, there's literally no time to waste. Run like you're being chased, fly like a bird escaping a trap!

Seriously, you lazy bum, go look at an ant. Just watch it for a sec; it'll teach you something. No one has to boss it around. It works hard all summer, stocking up on food for the winter. So how long are you gonna sleep in and do nothing? When are you getting out of bed? A little nap here, another one there, a day off here, another there, just chilling... you know what that leads to? A broke life. Poverty will be your new roommate, and it's not moving out.

Shady people and total liars talk out of both sides of their mouths. They give each other secret winks, tap their feet, and cross their fingers behind their backs. Their twisted minds are always scheming up something bad, always starting drama. But a disaster is coming for them, a total wreck, and their lives will be ruined with no way to fix it.
Here are six things God absolutely hates, and a seventh that He can't stand:

eyes that look down on everyone, a tongue that tells lies, hands that hurt innocent people, a heart that dreams up evil plans, feet that run to do wrong, a witness who lies in court, and someone who starts fights in their own family.

My friend, listen to your dad's advice; don't ignore what your mom taught you. Keep their words with you always, like a necklace you never take off. When you're walking, they'll guide you; when you're sleeping, they'll protect you; when you wake up, they'll give you wisdom for the day. Good advice is like a flashlight, solid teaching is a light, and being corrected is the road to real life.

They'll keep you away from the wrong kind of person, from the smooth talk of someone trying to tempt you. Don't get caught up in fantasizing about their looks, and don't fall for their flirty eyes. You might think a hookup is cheap, but getting involved with the wrong person can cost you everything—it can eat you alive. For real, can you hold fire in your lap and not get your clothes burned? Can you walk on hot coals and not get blisters? It's the same thing when you mess with someone else's partner. If you touch them, you're gonna pay the price. No excuses. Being hungry isn't an excuse for a thief to steal; when they're caught, they have to pay it all back, even if it means losing everything they own. Cheating is just a brainless move. It destroys your soul and yourself. You can expect to get beat up, get a black eye, and have your reputation totally ruined. A jealous husband is like a ticking time bomb of rage; he'll be out for revenge and won't show any mercy. Nothing you can say or pay will make it right; no amount of money or apologies will calm him down.

title: Don't Fall for the Ultimate Thirst Trap
paragraphs: Yo, my dude, listen up and lock in what I'm telling you. Seriously, treasure these instructions. If you do what I say, you'll be living your best life. My teaching is as precious as your own eyes—so guard it! Write it on the back of your hands, etch it into your heart. Treat Wisdom like she's your sister, and make Insight your bestie. They'll have your back and protect you from the Temptress—that girl with the smooth talk and honeyed words who's always trying to come to you secretly.

So, I was chilling at my window, looking out through the blinds, just watching the world go by. I saw this clueless young guy, totally without a clue, walking down the street where she lives and turning onto her path. It was getting dark, that time between evening and night when everything gets shadowy. And right on cue, this woman comes up to him. She was waiting for him, dressed to kill, you know? She was bold and loud, the type who can't sit still and is always out and about, never at home. You'd see her on the streets, at the mall, posted up on every corner.

She throws her arms around him, gives him a kiss, and grabs his arm like she owns him, saying, 'I've got a whole feast ready. I just made my offerings today, paid up all my vows. So I came out looking for you, hoping I'd run into you—and here you are! I've got fresh, clean sheets on my bed, super colorful and imported. My room smells amazing, like spices and exotic perfumes. Come on, let's just love all night. It'll be epic. My husband's out of town on a business trip and won't be back for like a month.'

Next thing you know, she's got him wrapped around her finger, totally mesmerized by her sweet talk. He's following her like a puppy, like a calf being led to the slaughterhouse. He's like a deer walking into a trap, about to get hit with an arrow. He's like a bird flying straight into a net, with no idea its freedom is over.

So listen up, my friends. Take what I'm saying seriously. Don't mess around with a woman like that. Don't even walk through her neighborhood. She's taken down countless victims; she's the end of so many guys. Her house is like a gateway to hell; she'll set you up with a coffin and a funeral shroud.

title: Wisdom Spills the Tea on How to Live Your Best Life
paragraphs: Yo, can you hear Lady Wisdom shouting out? Can you hear Madame Insight making some noise? She's right there at the main crossroads, the busiest spot in town. Right in the middle of the city square, where everyone's at, she's yelling, 'Yo, everyone, I'm talking to you! All you clueless people out there, get a grip and learn some common sense! You blockheads, it's time to shape up! You better listen up, 'cause I'm about to drop some serious knowledge on how to live your best life. My mouth chews and savors and relishes the truth—I can't stand even the taste of evil. Every word I say is legit and straight-up; no twisted or shady stuff. If you've got an open mind, you'll see it's all facts; if you're ready for the truth, you'll get it instantly. You should want my life-lessons more than you want to get rich, and knowing God is way better than any high-paying job. Seriously, Wisdom is worth more than all the expensive stuff you could ever want; nothing you could wish for is even in the same league.

I'm Lady Wisdom, and I'm basically besties with Sanity; Knowledge and Discretion are my neighbors. Fearing God means hating evil, and I absolutely despise all of that—pride, arrogance, and all that crooked talk. I've got the best advice and common sense on lock; I'm both Insight and the power to actually use it. With my help, leaders can actually rule, and lawmakers can make fair laws. With me, governors can govern, and so can anyone else in a position of real authority. I love the people who love me; if you're looking for me, you'll find me. Wealth and glory are my sidekicks, along with some serious honor and a great reputation. What I give you is worth way more than a huge paycheck, like, a ridiculously huge one; the rewards you get from me are better than any bonus you can imagine. You can find me on Righteous Road—that's my street—at the corner of Justice Avenue, handing out life to everyone who loves me, and I mean armloads of it!

God, in his infinite wisdom, made me first—the OG, the blueprint—before he did anything else. I was created a super long time ago, way before the Earth was even a thing. I showed up on the scene before the oceans, before the springs, rivers, and lakes. Before the mountains were even sculpted and the hills were formed, I was already there, a newborn. Long before God laid out the horizons of the Earth and got into the nitty-gritty of the soil and the weather, and before he put the sky in its place, I was there. When he drew the map and set the boundaries for the wild oceans, built the huge dome of the sky, and set up the fountains that fed the ocean, when he drew a line for the sea and put up a 'no trespassing' sign, and then laid out the foundations of the Earth, I was right there with him, making sure everything was perfect. Day after day, I was there, cheering him on, always loving his company, totally amazed by the world of things and creatures, and so happy about the human family.

So, my dear friends, listen up; the people who follow my ways are seriously blessed. Live a disciplined life and be wise; don't waste your precious life. Blessed is the man, blessed is the woman, who listens to me, who's awake and ready for me every morning, alert and responsive as I start my day. When you find me, you find life, like, real life, not to mention God's total approval. But if you do me wrong, you're only hurting yourself; when you reject me, you're flirting with death.

title: Wisdom vs. Folly: Choose Your Squad
paragraphs: Yo, so there's this super cool chick, Lady Wisdom. She's built this amazing house, like, it's got seven pillars and everything. She's prepped a massive feast: we're talking roasted lamb, the best wine, and a table that looks like it's straight out of a magazine with all the fancy silverware and flowers. She's sent out her crew and is now standing in the middle of town, shouting out to everyone who can hear: "Yo, you feelin' lost? Like you don't know what's up with life? Come hang with me, for real, I'm having a dinner party! I've got this incredible spread—fresh bread, roast lamb, top-shelf wine. Ditch your confusion and actually *live*! Come on, let's walk down this path to a life that actually means something."

But look, if you try to talk sense to some arrogant hater, you're just gonna get shut down. Try to call out someone's bad choices, and they'll come right back at you. So don't even waste your breath on someone who just wants to mock everything; you'll just get hurt. But it's a whole different story if you give advice to people who actually care about living right—they'll totally appreciate you for it. Share what you know with wise people, and they'll get even wiser. Tell good people what you know, and they'll get something out of it. A smart life starts with respecting God. You get real insight by knowing the Holy One. Lady Wisdom says, "It's because of me that your life gets deeper and you get to live a long, full life." So, if you live wisely, wisdom will be all up in your life. But if you make fun of life, life's gonna make fun of you right back.

And then you've got this other woman, this total party girl, Madame Prostitute. She's loud, clueless, and just messes around. She's just sitting on her front porch on the main street, and when people walk by, just trying to live their lives, she yells out, "Yo, you feelin' lost? Like you don't know what's up? Sneak away with me, I'll show you a good time! Nobody will find out—it'll be the best time of your life." But what they don't see are all the skeletons in her closet. All her guests? They end up in hell.

paragraphs: A wise kid makes their dad proud, but a foolish kid is a major bummer for their mom.
Money you get from cheating won't get you anywhere, but living an honest life lasts forever.
God's got the back of honest people, so they won't starve. But for the wicked, He'll make sure their cravings are never satisfied.
Being lazy will make you broke, but hard work brings in the cash.
It's smart to get your work done when you have the chance, but it's dumb to slack off when you should be grinding.
Living a good and honest life brings on the blessings, but the words of the wicked are like a dark hole of negativity.
A good life is remembered forever, but a wicked life leaves behind a nasty legacy.
A wise person listens to advice, but a fool is just going to mess everything up.
If you're honest, you can live without a worry in the world. But if you're shady, you'll definitely get caught.
Avoiding eye contact is a sign that trouble's coming, but being open and honest with people leads to peace.
The words of a good person are like a refreshing spring of water, but the words of the wicked are a pit of nastiness.
Hatred is always starting drama, but love is all about squashing the beef and moving on.
You'll hear some real wisdom from someone who's actually smart, but a clueless person just needs a reality check.
Wise people are always learning, and that's the real treasure. But know-it-alls just talk and talk, and it's a total waste of time.
Rich people feel safe because of their money, but for the poor, their lack of money is their downfall.
The reward for being a good person is an awesome life, but a bad person just ends up with a whole lot of sin.
If you live a disciplined life, you're on the right track. But if you ignore advice, you're going to be lost for good.
Liars secretly hold on to their hate, but fools are out there spreading rumors for everyone to hear.
The more you talk, the less truth comes out. Wise people know when to keep their mouths shut.
What a good person has to say is worth listening to, but the wicked just run their mouths and say nothing of value.
A good person's words can be a feast for a lot of people, but people who just talk nonsense are empty inside.
It's God's blessing that makes you truly rich, and nothing you do can top that.
A fool thinks causing trouble is a good time, but a smart person finds joy in wisdom.
The worst fears of the wicked will come true, but good people will get what they've been hoping for.
When a storm hits, the wicked are wiped out. But good people are standing on solid ground and don't even flinch.
A lazy worker is nothing but a headache. They're like vinegar in your mouth or smoke in your eyes.
Respecting God will give you a long and full life, but a wicked life is a short and miserable one.
The hopes of good people end in a party, but the plans of the wicked just blow up in their faces.
God is a solid foundation for a life lived right, but he's not impressed with a half-hearted effort.
Good people are here to stay—they can't be shaken. But the wicked are here one day and gone the next.
A good person's words are like a fresh stream of wisdom, but a foul mouth is like a disgusting swamp.
The words of a good person are a breath of fresh air, but the words of the wicked just pollute everything.

title: Real Ones vs. Fakers: The Ultimate Guide to Life
paragraphs: God is lowkey not a fan of cheating when you're doing business; he loves it when everything is fair and square.
Prideful people are headed for a major L, but the humble ones stand strong.
The integrity of honest people keeps them on the right path, but the sneakiness of crooks will be their own downfall.
A fat bank account won't help you when life gets messy, but living a life of integrity can get you through anything.
Good character makes life a smooth ride; a wicked life is a rough one.
Good character is your best defense; crooks get caught up in their own toxic desires.
When a wicked person dies, that's it for them—game over, no more second chances.
A good person gets saved from a lot of trouble, while a bad person walks right into it.
The careless words of the godless can destroy people, but the wisdom of the godly saves them.
When things go well for good people, the whole city celebrates; when the wicked crash and burn, the city has a party.
A city thrives when righteous people bless it, but evil talk can turn it into a ghost town real quick.
Talking trash about others is just heartless; a person with good sense knows when to stay quiet.
A gossip can't be trusted with a secret, but a person of integrity will never spill secrets.
Without good leadership, people lose their way; the more wise advice you get, the better your chances of success.
Making deals with strangers is a good way to get burned; if you keep your cool, you'll avoid making dumb decisions.
A graceful woman earns respect, but violent men only care about money.
When you're kind to others, you're helping yourself; when you're cruel, you're only hurting yourself.
Bad work gets you a bad outcome; good work gets you a solid reward.
Choose to be loyal to God and his people and you'll truly live; chase after evil and you'll end up with nothing.
God can't stand people with twisted hearts, but he absolutely loves those who have integrity.
Bet on this: the wicked will not get away with it, and God's people will come out on top.
A beautiful face on a person with an empty head is like a gold ring in a pig's snout. It's a total waste.
The desires of good people lead to good things, but the ambitions of the wicked end in anger and frustration.
The world of the generous person keeps getting bigger, while the world of the stingy person keeps getting smaller.
The one who blesses others will be blessed in return; those who help others will be helped themselves.
People will curse those who are greedy and hoard things for themselves, but they'll bless everyone who is fair and generous.
The one who looks for good will find it; but if you study evil, you'll become evil.
A life that's all about money and stuff is dead—a stump. But a God-shaped life is a flourishing tree.
If you take advantage of your family, you'll end up with nothing; it's just a stupid way to live, and everyone knows it.
A good life is like a tree that bears fruit; a violent life destroys people.
If even good people barely make it, what do you think will happen to the wicked?

title: Real Talk: How to Win at Life (and Not Be a Clown)
paragraphs: If you're into self-improvement, you've gotta be open to feedback. It's pretty dumb to brush off advice that could make you better.
A good person gets to feel God's approval, which is an awesome feeling. On the other hand, God wants nothing to do with people who are always scheming and being sneaky.
You can't build a solid life on a shaky foundation, it's like trying to stand in a swamp. But when your life is rooted in God, you're on solid ground and can't be moved.
A supportive partner can make their spouse feel alive and full of energy. But a partner who is cold and unfeeling is like a disease that slowly eats away at you from the inside.
The thoughts of good people lead to fairness and justice. But the plans of messed-up people are all about creating chaos and corruption.
The words of wicked people are like traps that can lead to death. But the words of good people can save lives.
Wicked people and their plans eventually fall apart and amount to nothing. But the families and homes of good people stay strong and last.
A person who speaks with wisdom and common sense will be respected. But people who are all talk and no substance are looked down on.
It's way better to be a normal person who works for a living than to act like you're a big shot but actually be broke and starving.
Good people are even kind to their pets and animals. But when bad people try to be 'nice,' it's usually fake and they end up being cruel anyway.

title: King Solomon's Guide to Not Messing Up
paragraphs: When you get a dinner invite from someone important, use your manners. Don't just wolf down your food or talk with your mouth full. And for real, control your appetite; don't stuff yourself.
Don't burn yourself out just trying to get rich; learn to chill. Money can honestly disappear in a second. It's like it grows wings and just flies away.

Don't take food from a cheapskate; don't expect them to be generous. They're as stingy with you as they are with themselves. They'll say, 'Go on, eat! Drink!' but they totally don't mean it. The tiny portion will make you sick when you realize the whole thing was just for show.
Don't waste your breath trying to explain things to fools; they'll just make fun of your wise words.
Don't secretly move property lines or scam orphans out of their land. They have a super powerful Defender who will totally have their back.
Get serious about learning and listen up to advice that's been tested and proven true.
Don't be scared to discipline your kids; a spanking isn't going to kill them. Actually, a good spanking might save them from something way worse than death.
My kid, if you grow up to be wise, I'll be so incredibly happy. My heart will literally be dancing and singing when you speak the truth.
Don't even for a second be jealous of people who don't care about God. Instead, be all about respecting God 24/7. That's where your real future is. Then you won't end up with nothing.

Hey, listen up, my kid—get wise and get your life pointed in the right direction. Don't get wasted on too much wine or get fat from eating too much. Drunks and gluttons end up broke, sleeping their lives away in old, ragged clothes.

Listen respectfully to your dad who raised you, and don't ignore your mom when she gets old. Buy the truth—don't sell it for anything, not for love or money. Buy wisdom, education, and insight. Parents are so happy when their kids turn out well; wise kids make their parents proud. So make your dad happy! Make your mom proud!
My kid, I need your full attention. Please, just do what I'm showing you.
A prostitute is like a bottomless pit; a woman who sleeps around can get you into deep trouble, fast. She'll take everything you have; she's worse than a whole gang of thieves.

Who's always down and depressed? Who's always full of self-pity? Who's always getting into fights for no reason? Whose eyes are all red and blurry? It's the people who stay up all night drinking, who take their drinking way too seriously. Don't just look at how fancy the wine is. Judge it by the hangover it gives you—the killer headache, the sick stomach. You really want to be seeing double and slurring your words, stumbling around like a drunk sailor? You'll be like, 'They hit me, but I didn't feel it. They beat me up, but whatever.' And then you'll say, 'As soon as I can think straight, get me another drink!'

title: Life Hacks from the Wisest Dude Ever
paragraphs: Don't be jealous of bad people or even want to hang out with them. All they think about is stirring up drama and making trouble.
Building a life is like building a house: you need wisdom to build it, understanding to make it strong, and knowledge to fill it with awesome things.
Being smart is way better than being strong; brains beat brawn any day. To win at life, you need a solid game plan and a squad of wise advisors.
Deep talks are totally lost on fools; they're clueless when the conversation gets real.
The person who's always scheming something shady gets a reputation as a major troublemaker. Fools are basically sin-making machines, and cynics just ruin beautiful things.
If you fall apart when things get tough, you weren't that strong to begin with.
Help people who are in trouble; don't just stand by. If you say, 'Not my problem,' do you really think that's a good excuse? God is watching, and He's not impressed by your weak excuses.
Just like honey is good for you, knowledge and wisdom are good for your soul. Get them, and your future is secure, your hope is solid.

Don't mess with good people's lives or try to one-up them. No matter how many times they get knocked down, people who are loyal to God get back up. The wicked, on the other hand, end up face-planting.
Don't laugh when your enemy fails; don't get hyped about their downfall. God might see it, get annoyed, and decide to help them instead.
Don't waste your time on show-offs or wish you had what the wicked have. They have no future; they're on a one-way street to nowhere.
Respect God and your leaders; don't be a rebel. Your life can get turned upside down without any warning, and you won't see it coming.
It's just plain wrong to let injustice slide.
Anyone who defends a guilty person will go down in history as a bad guy, but whoever calls out the wicked will be thanked and rewarded.
An honest answer is as comforting as a warm hug.
Get your work done first, then you can chill.
Don't gossip about your neighbors behind their backs. Seriously, no slander. And don't ever say, 'I'm gonna get back at you for what you did to me. I'll make you pay!'

I saw a lazy person's field and a slob's vineyard the other day. They were totally overgrown with weeds and the fences were all broken. It made me think, and I learned a lesson: a little nap here, a little break there, and before you know it, you're broke and poverty is your new roommate.

title: Solomon's Life Hacks, Pt. 2
paragraphs: Yo, here are some more wise words from Solomon, written down by King Hezekiah's crew.
God loves hiding little secrets in the world, and scientists get a kick out of finding them. It's like a huge game of hide-and-seek.
A legit leader's understanding is crazy wide and deep, like the sky or the ocean. They just get it.
You gotta get the gunk out of silver to make something beautiful. Same with leaders - get rid of the shady people, and you'll have a government you can actually trust, one that makes God look good.
Don't be that person trying way too hard to be the center of attention. It's way better to be invited to the honored section than to get kicked out for trying to sneak in.
Don't just assume the worst. There's probably a good reason for what you saw, so chill for a sec.
If you're in a heated argument, don't go spilling secrets. That news will spread everywhere, and then no one will ever trust you again.
Saying the right thing at the right time is like a perfectly chosen accessory. And when a wise friend calls you out, it's like they're giving you a sick piece of gold jewelry.
Friends who actually do what they say they'll do are as refreshing as an ice-cold drink on a blazing hot day.
Someone who talks a big game but never delivers is like a sky full of storm clouds that never actually rains. Just a whole lot of noise.
If you're patient and don't give up, you can get through to anyone. A gentle word can break down the toughest walls.
When someone gives you a whole box of chocolates, don't eat it all at once or you'll get sick. Same with friends - don't overdo it and hang out 24/7, or they'll get tired of you real quick.
Anyone who spreads lies about their friends is basically a walking disaster waiting to happen.
Trusting someone who's known for backstabbing is like chewing on a tooth that's already killing you. It's just asking for more pain.
Trying to cheer someone up with happy songs when they're feeling down is like pouring salt on a wound. Just... don't.
If you see your enemy is hungry, buy them some food. If they're thirsty, get them a drink. Your kindness will totally throw them off, and God will have your back.
A cold north wind means a storm is coming, and a gossipy person means you're about to see some angry faces.
It's honestly better to live by yourself in a tiny, busted apartment than in a mansion with someone who never stops complaining.
Getting a message from a friend you haven't heard from in forever is as refreshing as a cold drink when you're totally exhausted.
A good person who lets a bad person walk all over them is like a clean spring that's been turned to mud.
It's not a good look to eat candy all day, and it's not good for you to constantly be chasing praise and glory.
Someone with no self-control is like a house that's been completely wrecked, with no doors or windows to protect it.

title: Spitting Facts About Fools & Lazy People
paragraphs: Giving props to a fool is as pointless as wishing for a snow day in July or for rain when it's time to harvest.
You shouldn't be scared of a curse you don't deserve, any more than you'd be scared of a little bird flying by.
Horses need a whip, sailboats need a rudder, and fools, well, they need a good old-fashioned reality check.
Don't even try to argue with a fool's nonsense; you'll just end up looking like a fool, too.
But when you do have to answer a fool, keep it simple so they don't get a big head and think they're smart.
Trusting a fool to deliver a message is like asking for trouble. Seriously, just don't.
A proverb coming from a fool is as useless as a wet noodle.
Giving a fool a position of honor is like trying to build a marble pillar on a foundation of mud bricks. It's just not gonna work.
Asking a moron to drop some wisdom is like handing a drunk person a scalpel. It's a disaster waiting to happen.
Hiring a fool or a drunk is basically shooting yourself in the foot.
Just like a dog goes back to its own vomit (gross, I know), a fool just keeps repeating their same old dumb mistakes.
You see that person who thinks they're the smartest one in the room? A fool has more potential than them. For real.
Lazy people will make up any excuse to not do anything, like, "I can't go outside, there are tigers in the streets!" and then just roll back over in bed.
Just like a door just swings back and forth on its hinges, a lazy person just turns over and over in their bed.
A lazy person might get as far as putting their fork in the food, but they're too lazy to actually lift it to their mouth.
These dreamers think they're so important and smarter than everyone else, even a whole university faculty.
Jumping into a fight that has nothing to do with you is as dumb as grabbing a mad dog by the ears.
People who mess up on purpose and then say, "Just kidding, I didn't mean it!" are worse than someone who starts a forest fire and just walks away.
When you run out of wood, the fire dies. When the gossip stops, the drama ends.
A person who loves to argue is like throwing gasoline on a fire.
Listening to gossip is like eating junk food. Do you really want that garbage in your system?
Smooth talk from someone with a bad heart is like a pretty glaze on a cracked, useless pot.

Your enemy might act like your best friend, shaking your hand and being all nice, but they're just plotting against you. Don't fall for their sweet talk; they're just waiting for the right moment to backstab you. No matter how well they hide their true colors, eventually, everyone will see them for who they really are.
What goes around comes around. Malice will come back to bite you, and spite is a boomerang.
Liars hate the people they lie to, and people who flatter you are just trying to mess up your trust.

title: Real Talk on Friends, Haters, and Getting Your Life Together
paragraphs: Don't go bragging about your plans for tomorrow; you literally have no idea what's gonna happen.
Let other people hype you up; don't be the one tooting your own horn.
Trying to carry a giant log on your shoulders while lifting a massive rock is nothing, and I mean NOTHING, compared to how draining it is to deal with a fool.
Anger is a beast, and rage is a flood, but for real, who can even handle jealousy?
Getting called out to your face is way better than getting fake love that's never actually real.
The tough love from a real one is worth it; the kisses from an enemy will mess you up.
When you're full, you'll even turn down dessert. But when you're starving, you'd eat anything.
People who can't stay put and are always bouncing around are like birds that can't find a nest.
Just like lotion and a good scent make you feel good, a real friendship is super refreshing for your soul.
Don't ditch your friends or your parents' friends and run back to your family whenever things get hard. A friend who's close by is way better than family that's far away.
Get smart, my dude, and make me proud. Then I won't be stressing about anything the world throws at me.
A smart person sees trouble coming and avoids it. A clueless person just walks right into it and gets wrecked.
If you're loaning money to a stranger, make sure you get something as a guarantee. Be super careful about taking something from someone who's just passing through.
If you wake up your friend super early by yelling 'RISE AND SHINE!', it's gonna sound more like a curse than a friendly wake-up call.
A nagging partner is like a leaky faucet that just won't stop dripping. You can't turn it off, and you can't escape it.
You use iron to sharpen iron, and in the same way, one friend sharpens another.
If you take care of your apple trees, you'll get to eat the apples. If you respect your boss, you'll get respect back.
Just like water shows you your own face, your face shows what's in your heart.
Hell is never satisfied, and lust is the same way, it just never stops.
You test how pure silver and gold are by putting them in fire. You test people's hearts by giving them a little bit of fame.
You can try to beat the foolishness out of a fool, but it's never gonna work.

Know every single one of your sheep by name; take really good care of your flock. Don't just assume they'll always be there, 'cause nothing lasts forever, you know? And then, when you've harvested all the crops and stored them away, you can make sweaters from the lamb's wool and sell your goats for some cash. You'll have plenty of milk and meat to get your family through the winter.

title: Real Talk on Living Right vs. Getting Wrecked
paragraphs: Bad people are always paranoid, ready to bolt even when no one is chasing them. But good people are chill and confident, bold like lions.
When the country is a mess, everyone acts like they have the answers. But it takes a truly smart leader to actually fix things.
When a bad person with power picks on the poor, it's like a hailstorm that destroys all the crops. Total disaster.
If you ignore God's rules, you're basically saying yes to all kinds of messed-up stuff. But if you love God's rules, you'll fight to protect them.
Evil people just don't get what's right. But those who look for God understand it completely.
It's way better to be poor and honest than to be rich and a liar.
If you follow God's law, you'll get a reputation for being wise. But if you hang out with a wild crowd, you're just going to embarrass your parents.
If you get rich by cheating people, eventually someone who is a friend to the poor will come and give it all back to them.
If you refuse to listen to God, He's not going to listen to your prayers either.
If you lead good people down the wrong path, you're going to end up in a bad place. But if you do good things, you'll get rewarded for it.
Rich people think they're so smart, but a poor person with discernment can see right through their act.
When good people get promoted, it's a party for everyone. But when bad people are in charge, everyone hides.
You can't just hide your mistakes and expect to get away with it. You find forgiveness by owning up to them and quitting them.
A person with a soft heart is blessed, but a person with a hard heart is headed for a hard life.
A wicked ruler oppressing the poor is as scary as a roaring lion or a charging bear.
A leader who is clueless is also super abusive. But a leader who hates corruption has a bright future ahead.
A murderer who is haunted by guilt is basically doomed. You can't help them.
Live an honest life and you'll be safe and sound. But a crooked life will lead to ruin.
Work hard in your own field, and you'll have plenty of food. But if you just party all the time, you'll end up with nothing.
Hard work and consistency totally pay off. But those get-rich-quick schemes are just scams.
Playing favorites is never a good look. You can cause a lot of damage in ways that seem small.
A stingy person who's trying to get rich quick has no idea they're about to be broke.
In the long run, people appreciate it more when you call them out on their stuff than when you just flatter them all the time.
Anyone who robs their parents and says, 'What's the big deal?' is worse than a gangster.
A greedy person just starts drama, but trusting in God brings peace.
If you think you know everything, you're a fool. Real survivors learn from others.
Be generous to the poor and you'll never be in need. But if you ignore them, you'll get a ton of hate.
When bad people take over, good people go into hiding. But when the crooks get kicked out, it's safe for everyone to come out again.

title: Real Talk: How to Not Wreck Your Life
paragraphs: If you're one of those people who just hates being corrected and gets even more stubborn, a day's gonna come when your life just falls apart, and it'll be too late for anyone to help.
When good people are in charge, everyone's stoked, but when a bad leader is running things, everyone's miserable.
If you love being wise, you make your parents proud. But if you're running with prostitutes, you'll destroy their trust.
A leader with good judgment makes everything stable and secure; a leader who just uses people leaves a trail of destruction.
That neighbor who's always complimenting you is probably up to no good; they're likely just setting you up to take advantage of you.
Bad people get caught in their own traps, while good people see it coming, dodge it, and are glad they got away.
The righteous person actually gets what it's like to be poor; a heartless person has absolutely no clue.
A crew of cynics can bring down a whole city, but a group of wise people can chill everyone out.
When a wise person tries to argue with a fool, they just get laughed at and hit with sarcasm. It's a total waste of time.
Violent people hate honest folks, but moral people have their backs.
A fool just blurts out everything they're feeling, but a wise person thinks it over quietly first.
When a leader pays attention to toxic gossip, all their staff get infected with that same bad energy.
The poor person and the person who oppresses them have one thing in common: God gave them both the gift of sight.
When a leader makes sure to treat the poor and voiceless fairly, their authority gets stronger and they earn mad respect.
A little discipline teaches you wisdom; a spoiled kid just ends up embarrassing their parents.
When messed-up people are in charge, crime goes way up, but the good guys will get to see them fall in the end.
Discipline your kids, and you'll be so glad you did—they'll grow up to be awesome people to be around.
If people can't see what God's up to, they just end up tripping over themselves. But if you pay attention to what He shows you, you're seriously blessed.
It takes more than just words to get workers to listen; they'll just go in one ear and out the other.
Watch the people who always talk before they think—even a total idiot is better off than them.
If you let people walk all over you, you'll eventually just be forgotten.
Angry people stir up drama, and hot-headed people cause all sorts of trouble.
Pride will make you fall flat on your face, but being humble sets you up for honor.
If you team up with a criminal, you're basically turning on yourself. When things go down and people are crying for justice, you'll get cursed out too if you're too scared to speak up.
Being scared of what other people think will totally paralyze you. But trusting in God is the ultimate protection from that.
Everyone's trying to get on the leader's good side, but real justice only comes from God.
Good people can't stand to see deliberate evil; and wicked people can't stand to see genuine goodness.

title: 30 Things That Are Actually Mind-Blowing
paragraphs: The skeptic was like, "There's no God! No God! I can do whatever I want! I'm more animal than human; so-called human intelligence is beyond me.

"I totally failed 'wisdom.' I see no evidence of a holy God. Has anyone ever, like, climbed into Heaven and taken charge? Or grabbed the winds and controlled them? Or gathered the rains in a bucket? Or marked out the ends of the earth? Just tell me his name, and his sons' names. Come on, tell me!"
The believer replied, "Every promise of God is legit; he protects everyone who runs to him for help. So don't try to correct him; he might call you out and expose your lies."

And then he prayed, "God, I'm asking for two things before I die; please don't say no—Keep lies from my lips and liars out of my life. Give me just enough food to live on, not too much and not too little. If I'm too full, I might get arrogant and say, 'God? Who needs him?' If I'm poor, I might steal and bring shame to the name of my God."
Don't go tattling on your coworkers behind their backs; they'll accuse you of being sneaky, and then you'll be the one who looks guilty.
Don't curse your father or forget to bless your mother.
Don't think you're looking sharp when you haven't showered in weeks.
Don't be stuck-up and think you're better than everyone else.
Don't be greedy and cruel like a wolf, tearing into the poor and feasting on them, shredding the needy to pieces and leaving them for nothing.
A freeloader has twin daughters named "Gimme" and "Gimme more."
There are three things that are never satisfied, actually four that never say, "That's enough, thank you!"—
Hell, a barren womb, a parched land, and a forest fire.
An eye that disrespects a father and despises a mother—that eye will be plucked out by wild vultures and eaten by young eagles.
Three things blow my mind, no, four things I'll never get—
how an eagle soars in the sky, how a snake slithers over a rock, how a ship sails the ocean, and why teenagers act the way they do.
Here's how an adulteress operates: she sleeps with a stranger, washes up, then asks, "Who's next?"
Three things are too much for even the earth to handle, yeah, four things that shake its foundations—
when a janitor becomes the boss, when a fool gets rich, when a prostitute gets voted "woman of the year," and when a mistress replaces a faithful wife.
There are four small creatures that are the wisest of the wise—

ants—they're weak, but they stock up plenty of food for the winter; marmots—they're vulnerable, but they build their homes in solid rock; locusts—they have no leader, but they swarm over a field like an army; lizards—they're easy to catch, but they can sneak into a king's palace.
There are three who walk with dignity, four that are impressive to watch—
a lion, the king of beasts, who bows to no one; a proud, strutting rooster; a billy goat; and a king leading a royal procession.
If you're dumb enough to show off by offending people and being rude, don't be shocked when someone punches you in the face. Just like churning milk makes butter, stirring up anger leads to a fight.

title: Mom's Guide to Being a King & Finding a Queen
paragraphs: The advice King Lemuel got from his mom—some serious wisdom bombs:
"Listen up, my son, the child I bore, the son I dedicated to God! What are you even doing? Don't waste your strength on girls chasing after your status—promiscuous girls who shipwreck leaders.

"Leaders can't be out here making fools of themselves, getting wasted on wine and beer. If they're hungover, they can't tell right from wrong, and that ends up hurting the people who rely on them. Alcohol should be for people who are in serious pain, like a sedative for those who are suffering and feel like they're already dying.
"You need to speak up for those who can't speak for themselves, for the rights of all the outcasts. Be a voice for justice! Defend the poor and people who have nothing."

Finding a truly good woman is rare, and she's worth way more than diamonds. Her husband trusts her 100%, and he never regrets it. She's never petty and always treats him with kindness, her whole life. She's a savvy shopper, finding the best materials, and she actually enjoys making things. She's like a cool merchant ship, bringing back unique and amazing things from far away. She's up before the sun, making breakfast for her family and getting her day organized. She'll check out a piece of land and buy it, then use her own savings to plant a garden. First thing in the morning, she's dressed and ready for work, rolling up her sleeves and excited to get going. She knows her work has value, so she's not in a rush to clock out. She's a pro at all the home-related skills, a master of homemaking. She's always ready to help someone in need and reaches out to the poor. She doesn't stress when it snows because her family's winter clothes are all patched up and ready. She makes her own clothes, and they're not just functional—she wears stylish, colorful outfits. Her husband is a big deal, a respected leader in the community. She even has a side hustle, designing and selling clothes and sweaters to local shops. Her style is classic and well-made, and she's optimistic about the future. When she talks, she has something smart to say, and she says it with kindness. She keeps a close eye on her household, making sure everyone is being productive. Her kids look up to her and praise her, and her husband brags about her, saying, "A lot of women do amazing things, but you're on a whole other level!" Charm can be fake, and beauty doesn't last. The woman who truly deserves praise is the one who respects God. Give her the credit she deserves! Let her life be filled with praise.
